title: Faster Payments to Veterans' Survivors Act of 2022
official_summary:
Faster Payments to Veterans' Survivors Act of 2022

This act modifies policies and procedures related to the payment of benefits under certain life insurance programs administered by the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA).

If a primary beneficiary has not made a claim for payment within one year (currently two years) after the death of the insured under the National Service Life Insurance (NSLI) program or the United States Government Life Insurance (USGLI) program, the VA is authorized to make payment to another designated beneficiary as if the primary beneficiary had predeceased the insured. If no designated beneficiary makes a claim within two years (currently four years) after the death of the insured, the VA is authorized to make a payment to a person the VA deems to be equitably entitled to such benefit.

The act also modifies the beneficiary designation process under NSLI and USGLI. Specifically, if a person does not designate a beneficiary for insurance, or if the designated beneficiary predeceases the insured person, the VA must determine the beneficiary in a specified order of succession.

Additionally, the act requires the VA to improve its processes and procedures with respect to identifying, locating, and paying hard-to-find beneficiaries of life insurance policies, including by improving its website search tools.

summary.headline: This law speeds up VA payments on certain veterans' life insurance policies when beneficiaries are slow to claim or were never named.
summary.what_it_does: The law shortens the waiting periods the VA uses before paying life insurance benefits under two programs, NSLI and USGLI. If a primary beneficiary does not file a claim within one year after the insured person dies, the VA can pay another designated beneficiary as if the primary one had died first. If no designated beneficiary claims within two years, the VA can pay someone it finds equitably entitled to the benefit. The law also sets an order of succession for choosing a beneficiary when none was named or the named one has died, and requires the VA to improve how it finds and pays hard-to-find beneficiaries, including better website search tools.

who_it_affects.group: Beneficiaries named on NSLI or USGLI life insurance policies
who_it_affects.how: Primary beneficiaries have one year instead of two to file a claim before the VA can move payment to another designated beneficiary.

who_it_affects.group: Families of deceased veterans and insured service members with NSLI or USGLI policies
who_it_affects.how: Surviving relatives may receive payments sooner, and the VA can follow a set order of succession when no beneficiary was named or the named one has died.

who_it_affects.group: Other people the VA considers equitably entitled to policy benefits
who_it_affects.how: If no designated beneficiary claims within two years, the VA may pay a person it finds equitably entitled instead, where before the window was four years.

who_it_affects.group: Hard-to-find beneficiaries of VA life insurance policies
who_it_affects.how: The VA must improve its methods for identifying, locating, and paying these people, including its online search tools.
